RE in a Church of England School
As a Church of England school, Christianity has a central and significant place within our RE curriculum.
Children develop an increasingly rich understanding of the Christian story, Christian beliefs and theology, exploring key concepts and considering how these influence the lives of Christians today.
Importantly, children learn that Christianity is not one single experience or expression of faith.
They encounter Christianity as a diverse, global and living faith, considering how Christians from different traditions, cultures and communities may express and experience their faith in different ways.
Alongside Christianity, children encounter and develop meaningful knowledge of other religions and worldviews, helping prepare them to live with understanding, curiosity and respect in an increasingly diverse society.
All Saints Church – Faith in Our Community
Our relationship with All Saints Church, Brill is an important and valued part of school life.
The church provides children with a tangible connection between their classroom learning and a living Christian community.
Through visits to the church and opportunities to engage with local clergy and members of the church community, children can explore Christian worship, traditions, symbolism and practice within an authentic setting.
Our relationship with All Saints helps children understand that religion is not simply something found in a textbook – it is lived, experienced and expressed by people and communities.
Our village and church therefore provide an important local context for children’s developing religious literacy.
Knowledge, Enquiry and Big Questions
RE at Brill combines secure knowledge with thoughtful enquiry.
Children need knowledge in order to engage meaningfully with religious and philosophical questions. Key beliefs, concepts, vocabulary, texts, traditions and practices are therefore explicitly taught and revisited as children progress through school.
Alongside this knowledge, children are encouraged to ask questions and explore ideas.
They learn that some questions do not have one simple answer and that people may reach different conclusions depending upon their beliefs, experiences and worldview.
As children develop, we encourage them to move beyond simply describing what somebody believes towards considering:
Why might this be important?What difference might this belief make?How might different people understand this?What might influence someone’s beliefs?
This enables children to develop increasingly sophisticated religious and theological thinking.
Encountering Religion and Worldviews
Wherever possible, we want children to encounter religion as it is actually lived.
Children have opportunities to learn through sacred texts, artefacts, places of worship, visitors and first-hand experiences.
They encounter different religious and non-religious perspectives and learn that there can be diversity within a religion or worldview as well as differences between them.
Visits and experiences beyond our immediate community broaden children’s horizons and enable them to engage with beliefs and practices that may be less familiar to them.
This helps children develop the knowledge, confidence and vocabulary to discuss religion and belief with curiosity and respect rather than assumption.
Spiritual Development and Reflection
RE provides rich opportunities for children to explore questions of meaning, purpose, identity, belonging, morality and the nature of existence.
Children are given opportunities to reflect upon what they encounter and consider how it connects with their own experiences, questions and developing understanding of the world.
Reflection is not about expecting children to reach a particular conclusion.
Instead, we create space for children to wonder, question, consider and respond.
These opportunities contribute to children’s spiritual development and support our wider aspiration that every member of our school community should be able to flourish and experience life in all its fullness.
Our Christian Values
Our school values of Honesty, Hope, Courage and Compassion are rooted in our Christian vision and woven throughout the life of Brill School.
RE gives children opportunities to explore these and other values more deeply, considering how beliefs and teachings can influence the choices people make and the ways in which they treat others.
Children consider themes such as justice, responsibility, forgiveness, service, stewardship and compassion, encountering examples of people whose beliefs have inspired them to act.
They are encouraged not simply to know our values, but to consider what those values might look like when lived out in the real world.
Learning Beyond the Classroom
First-hand experiences are an important way of bringing children’s RE learning to life.
Alongside our strong relationship with All Saints Church, children have opportunities to encounter different faiths, traditions and places of worship through visits, visitors and experiences beyond school.
These opportunities help children connect classroom knowledge with real people and communities and recognise the diversity that exists both within and between religions.
They also provide valuable opportunities for children to ask questions, challenge assumptions and develop their understanding of Britain as a religiously and culturally diverse society.
Our SIAMS Journey
Our most recent SIAMS inspection recognised the strength of Brill’s Christian vision and the way in which it enables pupils and adults to flourish.
RE was recognised as a priority within the school, with a carefully planned, challenging and well-sequenced curriculum. Our children benefit from opportunities to explore a range of religions and worldviews and deepen their understanding through experiences beyond the classroom.
As a school committed to continual development, we continue to build upon these strong foundations.
In particular, we are continuing to strengthen children’s understanding of Christianity as a diverse and living world faith and developing opportunities for spirituality and reflection across our wider curriculum.
Our SIAMS journey is not something separate from everyday school life. It forms part of our continuing reflection upon who we are as a Church school and how our vision is lived out for every child.
Respectful Dialogue
RE provides children with important opportunities to practise disagreeing well.
Children learn to listen carefully to others, ask appropriate questions, explain their own thinking and recognise that people can hold different beliefs and perspectives while treating one another with dignity and respect.
We create classrooms in which children feel safe to explore ideas, ask difficult questions and express their own thoughts.
Children do not need to share the same beliefs in order to listen to, understand and respect one another.
This supports our aspiration to prepare children to participate thoughtfully and compassionately in a diverse and changing world.
An Inclusive RE Curriculum
RE is for every child at Brill, regardless of their own faith, worldview or background.
As a Church of England school, we proudly celebrate our Christian foundation while warmly welcoming children and families of all faiths and none.
Teachers use appropriate adaptations, vocabulary support, visual resources, artefacts and experiences to enable all pupils, including those with SEND and additional needs, to engage meaningfully with important religious concepts.
Children who demonstrate secure understanding are challenged to make increasingly sophisticated connections, consider different interpretations and construct thoughtful, well-reasoned responses.
Every child’s questions and contributions are valued.
IMPACT
By the end of their Brill journey, we want our children to be knowledgeable, curious and respectful thinkers who can engage confidently with questions of religion, belief and worldview.
We want children to leave Brill able to:
Most importantly, we want children to leave Brill understanding that belief matters – whether that is religious belief, a non-religious worldview or the values and ideas through which people make sense of their lives.
We want them to have the knowledge to understand others, the confidence to ask difficult questions and the compassion to listen when somebody’s answer is different from their own.
Through RE, we want our children to look beyond themselves, think deeply and engage thoughtfully with the wonderfully diverse world in which they live.
“With the wind in our sails, we shall live ‘life in all its fullness’.”
Be Bold. Be Brave. Be Brill-iant.

pageCache.pageTitle: Reading at Brill - Brill Church of England School
pageCache.text:
Reading at Brill
At Brill, we believe that reading is the foundation of a child’s education and the key to unlocking a lifetime of learning. Our aim is for every child to develop a genuine love of reading, enjoy a wide range of high-quality literature, and become confident, fluent readers who understand the value and pleasure that reading brings.
This journey begins in the Early Years, where children learn to read through the Supersonic Phonic Friends programme within an immersive, language-rich environment. It continues throughout the school, culminating in Year 6, where pupils become independent readers and even help to run our school library, inspiring and supporting younger children.
Reading is taught explicitly through daily Guided Reading lessons, regular one-to-one and small-group reading opportunities, and carefully chosen texts that inspire curiosity, develop vocabulary and promote high-quality writing.
We value the vital role that families play in supporting reading and encourage parents and carers to read with their children every day whenever possible.
If you have any questions about your child’s reading journey, please speak to their class teacher in the first instance or contact the English Lead using the details on this page.
Early Reading and Phonics
Children in the Early Years and Key Stage One learn to read using the Supersonic Phonic Friends programme. This systematic, structured approach develops secure phonics knowledge and provides children with fully decodable reading books that are carefully matched to their stage of learning, helping them build confidence, fluency and a love of reading.
Supersonic Phonic Friends is taught through a cast of memorable characters, each representing a different aspect of phonics learning. These characters help children understand and remember important concepts, making learning both meaningful and enjoyable. Through stories, actions and consistent visual cues, children develop confidence in recognising sounds, reading words and spelling accurately.
Who is who and what do they do Download (pdf)
Alongside their decodable books, children enjoy a wide range of high-quality texts, ensuring they develop both the technical skills needed to read and a genuine enjoyment of books.
Our Supersonic Phonic Friends Progression document shows the order in which children learn new sounds, tricky words and phonics skills throughout the programme. It helps parents understand what their child is learning at each stage and provides a useful guide for supporting reading and phonics practice at home, ensuring school and home work together to build confident, successful readers.
Supersonic Friends Progression Map Download (pdf)
Literacy Coordinator a.butler@brillschool.org.uk
We use the Solomon Kingsnorth approach for our guided reading sessions to develop confident, thoughtful and enthusiastic readers. This approach places high-quality, challenging texts at the centre of reading lessons and encourages children to read, think and discuss deeply.
Children read complete texts or carefully selected extracts together, enabling them to build reading stamina, develop fluency and explore increasingly complex vocabulary and ideas. Teachers model expert reading, demonstrating how skilled readers make sense of a text by questioning, predicting, summarising, clarifying and making connections. Rich classroom discussion plays a central role, allowing pupils to articulate their ideas, listen to others and refine their thinking.
Vocabulary instruction is woven throughout every lesson. Children explore ambitious words in context, discuss shades of meaning and learn how authors' language choices influence the reader. This explicit focus on vocabulary supports both reading comprehension and children's own spoken and written language
As a school we have a range of texts to support children and their reading development and these are categorised by the spellings for the sounds they contain.
All reading books are matched to the sounds children have covered in school to ensure we maximise their ability to apply their new knowledge and these books are read both within school and then sent home for children to further embed the skills.
Most children move on to our library's Early Reader and then Free Reader collections once they are reading fluently and have completed the phonics programme.
Reading for pleasure is at the heart of everything we do. We strive to foster a lifelong love of books through engaging teaching, carefully selected texts and a vibrant reading culture across the school.
Our welcoming library provides children with access to a rich variety of fiction, non-fiction and poetry, while our dedicated library team supports pupils in selecting books that both motivate and challenge them. Weekly special reading sessions, author visits and a range of reading events further encourage children to discover the joy of reading.
At Brill, reading aloud is a valued and protected part of every school day because we know it is one of the most powerful ways to inspire a lifelong love of reading. Teachers regularly share carefully chosen, high-quality texts that introduce children to new authors, genres and ideas, many of which they may not yet be able to access independently. These shared reading experiences help to build a community of readers, spark meaningful discussion and foster a love of books. Reading aloud also broadens children's vocabulary, deepens their understanding of language and provides rich models of writing that inspire and support learning across the curriculum.
At Brill, we believe that some of the best reading recommendations come from children themselves. Brill's Best Books is a whole-school initiative that celebrates reading for pleasure while giving pupils the opportunity to become reading ambassadors for their peers.
When a child finishes a book that they feel is truly special, they are invited to write a short recommendation explaining why they think it deserves to be recognised as one of Brill's Best Books. They reflect on what they enjoyed about the story, the characters, the author's writing style or the themes explored, helping them to think more deeply about their reading.
Once their recommendation is complete, the book is awarded a Brill's Best Books sticker and proudly displayed in our dedicated library collection. This growing display showcases a wide range of pupil-recommended books and provides inspiration for other children looking for their next great read.
Our 'Page Turners' are a team of enthusiastic Key Stage 2 pupils who are elected by their peers to champion reading across the school. They play an important role in promoting a love of books and helping to create a vibrant reading culture for all children.
Each week, our Reading Leaders visit classrooms to share carefully chosen stories with younger pupils, modelling fluent, expressive reading and inspiring children to discover new books and authors. They also work alongside staff to develop exciting new ideas and initiatives that celebrate reading throughout the school, helping to ensure that reading remains at the heart of life at Brill.
How to Support Reading at Home
The Open University have a great website that also provides parents with practical advice and ideas to support their child's reading journey at home. It offers guidance on how to encourage a love of reading, develop reading confidence and make shared reading an enjoyable part of everyday life.

Science
What does Science look like at Brill?
At Brill Church of England School, we want children to be curious about the world around them and confident in asking questions about how and why things happen.
Science gives children the opportunity to explore, investigate, observe, question and make sense of the natural and physical world. We want our pupils to develop strong scientific knowledge while also learning how scientists think and work.
Science forms part of our Brill Horizons curriculum and is supported by Cornerstones Maestro, providing a carefully sequenced progression of knowledge and skills from the Early Years through to Year 6.
Our beautiful rural setting, school grounds and opportunities for outdoor learning provide a rich environment in which children can experience science beyond the classroom and see their learning come to life.
INTENT
Our Science curriculum is ambitious for every child.
We want children to develop a secure body of scientific knowledge while nurturing the curiosity, creativity and investigative thinking that sit at the heart of science.
Children are encouraged to ask questions, make predictions, investigate ideas, notice patterns and use evidence to develop explanations.
Our curriculum develops both:
Substantive knowledge – the scientific facts, concepts, models and ideas children need to understand the world;
Disciplinary knowledge – understanding how scientific knowledge is developed through observation, investigation, testing, measurement, analysis and evaluation.
Through our Science curriculum, we aim for children to:
We want children to understand that science is not simply a collection of facts that we already know. It is a way of questioning, investigating and continually developing our understanding of the world.
Our children are encouraged to be bold in asking questions, brave in testing their ideas and Brill-iant in using evidence to explain what they discover.

Brill Horizons and Cornerstones Maestro
Science is taught through our Brill Horizons curriculum, supported by Cornerstones Maestro.
Learning is carefully sequenced so that children’s scientific knowledge and understanding build progressively from their earliest experiences in the Early Years through to Year 6.
Children revisit important concepts over time, allowing them to make connections with previous learning and develop increasingly sophisticated understanding.
Our Brill Horizons Big Ideas support children in recognising these connections. Concepts including Nature, Investigation, Processes, Change, Materials and Comparison are particularly significant within Science and recur throughout children’s learning.
This enables pupils to see how individual units of learning connect to a much bigger understanding of the world around them.

Children are taught how to work scientifically, with expectations becoming increasingly sophisticated as they progress through the school.

Knowledge and Vocabulary
Secure scientific knowledge provides the foundation for successful investigation and reasoning.
Key knowledge and vocabulary are explicitly taught, revisited and applied throughout children’s learning.
Teachers make connections with previous learning so that children increasingly understand how scientific ideas relate to one another rather than experiencing each topic in isolation.
Children are encouraged to use precise scientific vocabulary when talking and writing about their learning and to explain their ideas using evidence and increasingly sophisticated scientific language.
Science in the World Around Us
Science is everywhere – and we want children to recognise that.
Our location provides wonderful opportunities to take scientific learning beyond the classroom.
Our school grounds, Forest School experiences and the wider rural environment around Brill enable children to observe seasonal change, explore habitats, investigate plants and living things and develop an appreciation of the natural world on their doorstep.
Where appropriate, learning is further enriched through practical experiences, visitors, trips and links with other areas of our Brill Horizons curriculum.
Children are encouraged to recognise how science helps us understand issues that affect their lives and their futures – from health and technology to biodiversity, sustainability and our changing environment.
Scientists and Scientific Careers
We want children to understand that science is a living, evolving subject shaped by people.
Throughout their time at Brill, children encounter scientists from different periods, backgrounds and fields of study. They learn about significant scientific discoveries and consider how scientific understanding has changed over time as new evidence has emerged.
Children are also introduced to the many ways in which science is used beyond school.
By encountering a diverse range of scientists, careers and applications of science, we want every child to recognise that science is something in which they can participate and a field in which they could have a future.
An Inclusive Science Curriculum
Science is for every child at Brill.
Teachers use appropriate adaptations, resources, representations and practical experiences to enable all pupils, including those with SEND and additional needs, to engage successfully with important scientific concepts.
Where children demonstrate secure understanding, challenge comes through deeper thinking, making connections, applying knowledge and increasingly sophisticated scientific reasoning, rather than simply moving on to new content.
We want every child to experience the excitement of discovery and see themselves as capable of thinking scientifically.
Science Across Brill Horizons
Science naturally connects with many other areas of our curriculum.
Children apply mathematical knowledge when measuring, collecting and interpreting data. They use their English skills to read scientific information, discuss ideas and communicate findings. Geography develops their understanding of environments and sustainability, while Design and Technology gives children opportunities to apply scientific understanding in practical contexts.
These connections help children recognise that knowledge does not sit within isolated subjects.
Instead, our Brill Horizons curriculum encourages children to connect what they know, build upon previous learning and use that knowledge to understand the world more deeply.
IMPACT
By the end of their Brill journey, we want our children to see themselves as curious, knowledgeable and confident young scientists.
We want children to leave Brill able to:
Most importantly, we want children to leave Brill with their curiosity intact.
We want them to continue noticing the world around them, asking “Why?”, wondering “What if?” and having the knowledge and confidence to investigate “How could we find out?”
Be Bold. Be Brave. Be Brill-iant.

Assistant Head / SENDCo / Inclusion Lead / Deputy DSL
Our Approach to Special Educational Needs at Brill
At Brill School we believe that the best support we can provide for all children, including those with additional needs, is to prepare them for life beyond Brill C of E School. All children face challenges of varying kinds whether they be as a direct result of learning needs, processing difficulties, emotional needs or other high incidence SEN needs that may have a 'label' or a diagnosis. Our approach is a holistic one where we aim to help the children to understand any particular barriers they may have and then focus on strategies to support them with these additional difficulties.
We believe that there is a fine balance between supporting our children with identified needs and ensuring that children receive the important message that they can achieve their best whatever their needs. We aim to recognise what are genuine difficulties for our children but we also have the intent to enable our children to feel positive about themselves. We believe that no one is defined by their 'need'. Everyone is an individual. As far as is possible, support is discrete and aims to boost confidence and promote a positive mindset. Our greatest successes have been when children have grown in confidence about themselves and have developed (with support) their own strategies to cope with particular difficulties they encounter as a result of their additional needs. We also recognise that areas of 'additional need' may also result in other particular areas of strength for those children. We celebrate our differences and recognise all of our children are individuals and at Brill are treated as such.

The children who work with Primrose look forward to her visit each week and love giving her lots of belly rubs and a good old brush!

Primrose the therapy dog, is a valued part of our SEND provision, helping to create a nurturing, inclusive environment where every child can thrive and live life to the fullest.

Organisation
As a Church of England school we will provide a daily act of collective worship which is based on Christian principles. Acts of Collective Worship are inclusive of pupils with all abilities and backgrounds of all pupils and allow those pupils from non-Christian families to join in. In order to achieve this there will be:
Collective Worship Timetable
Monday: Whole school vision and values themed Worship, led by Mrs Smith
Tuesday: Whole school Christian Worship, led by Gemma and Jenny.
Wednesday: Class Collective Worship, led by class teacher.
Thursday: Whole school singing themed Worship, led by Mrs Smith and Mr Dickson.
Friday: Whole school learning celebration themed Worship, led by Mrs Smith.
There are a group of Year 6 children who have the responsibility of preparing and supporting within Collective Worship on a daily basis by leading in prayer at the end of each collective worship. These children are known as our ‘Collective Crew’.
Prayer Space
Every year Reverend Jenny Edmans coordinates a fantastic Prayer Space week held either at Brill School, or All Saints Church in the village. The setting is transformed into a calm, tranquil and reflective space where all our pupils take part in reflective and thought provoking activities. There is a huge amount of community and church support, a variety of people come in during this week to lead and support our pupils in these enriched activities that develop and provoke the children’s spiritual, moral, social and cultural understanding and learning. Our community are involved and invited to come in towards the end of the week too.
